recall.minute: Model-based RL uses a model (distribution or sample) to plan: improve a policy from simulated experience, using the same backups as learning. Dyna-Q integrates direct RL, model learning and planning: after each real Q-learning update it stores Model(S, A) = (R, S′) and performs n simulated updates from previously seen pairs; in a 6×9 maze, planning (n = 50) cuts episode 2 from ~605 to ~45 steps and episodes 10–50 average 16.5 vs 41.5 steps. Dyna-Q+ adds κ√τ to rewards of long-untried transitions so changed environments are re-explored. UCB1 (Q + c√(ln N/n)) applied at each tree node is UCT: Q = 0.6, c = 1.41, N = 100 gives 1.557 for n = 10 and 2.74 for n = 2. MCTS iterates selection, expansion, simulation and backup and plays the most visited move; random rollouts limit it in deep positions. AlphaGo used supervised and RL policy networks, a value network and MCTS; AlphaGo Zero and AlphaZero learned from self-play alone; MuZero learns a latent model. World models (PlaNet, Dreamer) allow training in imagination, but model bias and compounding errors call for short rollouts, ensembles and real-data correction.
